package_info.package_versions: unknown (all versions distributed by Moonstone Sleet)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is distributed as part of a targeted social engineering campaign, masquerading as coding test assignments or games. Upon installation or import, it decrypts and executes a concealed malware loader (SplitLoader), which enables further payload execution, data exfiltration, credential theft, and potential ransomware deployment. This behavior is highly atypical for legitimate npm packages and poses significant risk to users.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code reads an encrypted payload from disk, decrypts it using a key from an environment variable, writes the decrypted payload to disk, and executes it, resulting in arbitrary code execution and enabling further malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code automatically decrypts and executes a hidden binary payload as soon as the package is imported, which is a hallmark of malware loaders and not expected in legitimate npm packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not decrypt and execute concealed binaries during import; legitimate packages should not perform arbitrary code execution without explicit user action or consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers or updaters may unpack and run binaries, but not in the context of a coding test or game package, and never silently at import-time.
key_indicators: Decryption of an encrypted payload file (payload.enc) using a key from environment variables
Writing and executing a binary (payload.exe) from JavaScript code at import-time
Use of child_process.execFile to launch a newly written executable
No user interaction or consent required for execution

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after execution of the decrypted payload, the code collects user information, environment variables, and sensitive files, then exfiltrates this data to a remote command-and-control server via HTTPS POST, resulting in credential and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code systematically collects sensitive user data and environment variables, accesses specific files from the user's Documents directory, and transmits this information to an external, attacker-controlled server without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages or their payloads should not access user documents or environment variables and transmit them externally, especially without explicit user consent or a clear, trusted business purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise backup or support tools may collect diagnostic data, but only with explicit user consent and transmission to trusted, documented endpoints—not to untrusted or unknown domains.
key_indicators: Access to user files in personal directories (e.g., Documents/important.docx)
Collection of environment variables and user information
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled domains (malicious-c2.com)
No user interaction or notification prior to exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Victim installs or imports the malicious npm package (SplitLoader variant) under the guise of a coding test or game.
attack_chain.leads_to: Decryption and execution of the next-stage payload (payload.exe), enabling arbitrary code execution.

attack_chain.action: The decrypted payload (malware loader) is executed, which collects sensitive data and exfiltrates it to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data theft, credential compromise, and potential further malware or ransomware deployment.

behavioral_signatures: Decryption and execution of hidden payloads (e.g., payload.enc) at import-time by npm packages
Access to user files in personal directories (e.g., Documents/important.docx) and environment variables by package code or spawned binaries
Network connections to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains immediately after package installation or import
file_indicators: Presence of payload.enc or similarly named encrypted payload files in npm package directories
Unexpected binary files (e.g., payload.exe) written and executed by JavaScript code in the package directory
References to environment variables (e.g., PAYLOAD_KEY) used for decryption in package code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the package's legitimate function, such as malicious-c2.com
Connections to attacker infrastructure (e.g., malicious-c2.com) following npm package installation or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations and imports for code that decrypts and executes binaries, especially if triggered at import-time. Flag packages that access user files in personal directories or environment variables and transmit data externally. Scan for the presence of encrypted payload files (e.g., payload.enc) and unexpected binaries (e.g., payload.exe) in package directories. Use network monitoring to detect suspicious outbound connections to known malicious domains (e.g., malicious-c2.com) after package installation or import. Correlate these behaviors to identify malicious loader activity.
